name: Mercor
h1_tail: Funding Rounds, Share Prices and Ownership
description: Mercor is privately held and has no ticker. Review the price of each funding round, the investors and SPVs that hold its shares, and the points to confirm before buying or selling.
ledes: Mercor is a privately held company that supplies human expertise for training and evaluating artificial intelligence models. Its shares are not listed on an exchange and have no quoted market price; the principal public reference points are the prices at which the company has raised capital. Its most recent financing, a $750 million Series D round announced on November 10, 2026, valued the company at $20 billion.

Based in San Francisco, Mercor engages professionals with specialized knowledge as contractors who help AI laboratories and other companies train and test their models. Existing shares change hands in privately negotiated transactions, frequently through special purpose vehicles, and remain subject to the company's transfer restrictions.
figs: Special purpose vehicles with SEC filings naming Mercor
table_note: Valuations are as reported at the time of each round. Mercor said the Series D included a tender offer for employees but did not disclose the size of the tender.
round_notes: Mercor did not name a lead investor for the Series D. In announcing the round on November 10, 2026, the company said that more than five million experts were part of its network; that figure is the company's own.

A round price reflects what investors paid for the preferred stock issued in that round. Most shares sold by employees are common stock, which carries fewer rights and typically trades at a discount to the preferred price.
investors: Mercor named Benchmark, Felicis, General Catalyst, Nvidia, Salesforce, Zoom, Sapphire Ventures and funds managed by affiliates of Apollo among the investors in the Series D. Felicis led the Series C and the Series B, and Benchmark led the Series A. Other investors include Robinhood Ventures, DST Global, Menlo Ventures and Peter Thiel.
spv_sentence: Since 2025, six special purpose vehicles formed to invest in Mercor have filed with the SEC, two of them in 2026.
sources: Sources: Mercor's announcements of its Series D (November 10, 2026), Series C (October 27, 2025) and Series B (February 20, 2025); reports by TechCrunch (February 2025), CNBC (February 2025) and Staffing Industry Analysts (September 2024); and SEC Form D filings.
